question: What is the maximum lump sum group life cover a member can have?

result.question: What is the maximum lump sum group life cover a member can have?
result.answer: The maximum lump sum group life cover per member is R25 000 000, regardless of salary or multiple. This is the maximum cover amount; it is not the same as the free cover limit, which is the amount covered without medical evidence and depends on the size band of the scheme.

hit.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
hit.text: Kestrel Group Life Assurance pays a lump sum to a member's nominated beneficiaries if the member dies while covered under a participating employer's scheme. Cover is provided under a group policy issued to the employer or retirement fund.

hit.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
hit.text:
- Members must be permanent employees of the participating employer.
- The maximum entry age is 64. Cover ends at the scheme's normal retirement age, or age 65 at the latest.
- Members must be actively at work on the date cover starts. If not, cover starts on the date they return to full duties.

question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?

result.question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?
result.answer: The application to continue life cover must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000, and no medical evidence is required. This is the group life continuation option — the member applies for an individual Kestrel policy.

citations.label: c1
citations.quote: A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age may apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.
citations.supports: Time limit of 60 days from leaving service, and the lower of group cover and R5 000 000, with no medical evidence required.
citations.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

caveats: The documents describe the continuation option for life cover only; the excerpts shown do not state a continuation option for disability income or funeral cover.

hit.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
hit.text:
A member who leaves the employer's service before normal retirement age may apply to continue their life cover on an individual Kestrel policy without providing medical evidence. The application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000.
Also written as: 5000000, R5000000

hit.title: Underwriting Free Cover Limits (effective 1 January 2026)
hit.text:
1. Schemes with fewer than 10 members are fully underwritten; no free cover limit applies.
2. The free cover limit is set at scheme inception and reviewed at each annual review date based on the number of members at that date.
3. Cover above the free cover limit requires medical evidence and is subject to underwriting acceptance.
4. Free cover limits apply only to members who are actively at work when cover starts.

question: What is the group life free cover limit for a scheme with 320 members?

result.question: What is the group life free cover limit for a scheme with 320 members?
result.answer: For a scheme with 320 members, the group life free cover limit is R5 000 000. That is Band 4, which covers 250 to 499 members; the limit is set at scheme inception and reviewed at each annual review date based on the number of members at that date, and free cover limits apply only to members who are actively at work when cover starts. Cover above the free cover limit requires medical evidence and is subject to underwriting acceptance.

question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?

result.question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?
result.answer: Under Option C the member would get R42 500 a month: 100% of the first R20 000 of monthly salary, plus 75% of the remaining R30 000. That is well under the R300 000 maximum monthly benefit, and salary means the member's monthly pensionable salary on the date disability started. This illustrates the general rule only — the claims team decides actual claims.

question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?

result.question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?
result.answer: The disability income benefit is paid monthly in arrears until the earliest of the member's recovery, the member's death, or the member reaching age 65 — so age 65 is the latest, and it stops sooner on recovery or death.

question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?

result.question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?
result.answer:
For a disability claim you need: a completed Kestrel disability claim form (with both the employer section and the member section), a medical report from the treating doctor, the member's last 3 payslips, and a certified copy of the member's ID document.

Claims can be submitted by the employer or broker through the Kestrel Broker Portal, or by email to claims@kestrel-assurance.example, and should be submitted no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period. Disability claims may take longer than the 10 working day target for group life claims, because medical information may need to be obtained.

question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?

result.question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?
result.answer: On Option C a member with a monthly salary of R50 000 would get R42 500 a month: 100% of the first R20 000 plus 75% of the remaining R30 000. That is under the R300 000 maximum monthly benefit for Option C, and the benefit is paid after a 3-month waiting period, escalating at a fixed 5% a year.

question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?

result.question: Until what age is the disability income benefit paid?
result.answer: The monthly benefit is paid until the earliest of: the member's recovery, the member's death, or the member reaching age 65 — so age 65 is the latest it runs, not a fixed term.

citations.supports: The benefit stops at the earliest of recovery, death or age 65, so age 65 is the maximum.
citations.title: Group Disability Income Benefit Product Guide (Version 2026.1)

question: What is the premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members?

result.question: What is the premium rate per R1 000 of life cover for a scheme with 150 members?
result.answer: The documents do not give a premium rate per R1 000 of life cover, and they do not set premium rates by scheme size. The group life guide says premiums are expressed as a percentage of the total annual salary bill of covered members, guaranteed for 2 years from the scheme commencement or review date and then reviewed based on scheme experience. For an actual rate, the broker or the underwriting team would need to be asked.
result.reason: The documents do not state a premium rate per R1 000 of life cover, nor any premium rate linked to the number of members in a scheme; they only say premiums are a percentage of the total annual salary bill. A broker or the underwriting team can quote the rate for a specific scheme.

result.question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?

question: What is the maximum lump sum group life cover a member can have?

result.question: What is the maximum lump sum group life cover a member can have?
result.answer: The maximum lump sum group life cover per member is R25 000 000, and it applies regardless of the member's salary or multiple. question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?

result.question: A member is leaving their employer. How long do they have to take up the continuation option, and up to what amount of cover?
result.answer: If the member leaves service before normal retirement age, the application must be received within 60 days of leaving service. Cover under the continuation option is limited to the lower of the member's group cover and R5 000 000, and no medical evidence is needed. This rule is for life cover; the documents shown do not state a continuation option for disability income cover.

hit.title: Underwriting Free Cover Limits (effective 1 January 2026)
hit.text:
1. Schemes with fewer than 10 members are fully underwritten; no free cover limit applies.
2. The free cover limit is set at scheme inception and reviewed at each annual review date based on the number of members at that date.
3. Cover above the free cover limit requires medical evidence and is subject to underwriting acceptance.
4. Free cover limits apply only to members who are actively at work when cover starts.

question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?

result.question: Under disability Option C, what monthly benefit would a member earning R50 000 a month receive?
result.answer: Under Option C, a member earning R50 000 a month would get R42 500 a month: 100% of the first R20 000 of monthly salary (R20 000) plus 75% of the remaining R30 000 (R22 500). That is below the option's R300 000 maximum monthly benefit. This applies once the 3-month waiting period has been completed, and "salary" means the member's monthly pensionable salary at the date disability started. This illustrates the general rule for these figures; the claims team decides individual claims.

question: Is there a waiting period on extended family funeral cover?

result.question: Is there a waiting period on extended family funeral cover?
result.answer: Yes, for extended family members there is a 6-month waiting period, but it applies only to death from natural causes — death from accidental causes is covered immediately. There is no waiting period for the main member, spouse and children.

question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?

result.question: What documents are needed to submit a disability claim?
result.answer: For a disability claim you need: a completed Kestrel disability claim form (both the employer section and the member section), a medical report from the treating doctor, the member's last 3 payslips, and a certified copy of the member's ID document. Claims should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period.

result.question: How long does Kestrel take to make a decision on a group life claim?

hit.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
hit.locator: section "How long does it take to assess a claim?"
heading_path: How long does it take to assess a claim?
hit.text: Kestrel aims to make a decision on group life claims within 10 working days of receiving all required documents. Disability claims may take longer because medical information may need to be obtained. Funeral claims are paid within 48 hours of receiving complete documents.

hit.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
hit.locator: section "How do I submit a claim?"
heading_path: How do I submit a claim?
hit.text: Claims can be submitted by the employer or broker through the Kestrel Broker Portal, or by email to claims@kestrel-assurance.example.

hit.title: Group Disability Income Benefit Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
heading_path: Group Disability Income Benefit: Product Guide
hit.text: Claims should be submitted as soon as possible and no later than 3 months after the end of the waiting period. See the Kestrel Claims FAQ for the documents required.

hit.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
hit.locator: section "What if I am unhappy with a claim decision?"
heading_path: What if I am unhappy with a claim decision?
hit.text: You can ask for the decision to be reviewed by writing to complaints@kestrel-assurance.example within 90 days of the decision. If you are still not satisfied, you may refer the matter to the long-term insurance ombud.

hit.title: Claims Frequently Asked Questions (updated March 2026)
hit.locator: section "Can I check the status of a claim?"
heading_path: Can I check the status of a claim?
hit.text: Yes. Employers and brokers can track claims on the Broker Portal. Members can call the Kestrel Client Centre on 0800 000 000 (fictitious number), Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00.

hit.title: Group Life Assurance Product Guide (Version 2026.1)
hit.text: The death of a member must be notified to Kestrel within 6 months of the date of death. Claims notified later may be declined. See the Kestrel Claims FAQ for the documents required.

hit.title: Group Funeral Benefit Scheme Rules (Version 2026.1)
hit.text: Funeral claims are paid within 48 hours of Kestrel receiving all the required documents.
